title: Florida barbershops: BS owner candidates held without a public contact source
hypothesis: A current Florida DBPR BS establishment row whose address line 1 parses as a person can supply a named barbershop-owner candidate, but the extract has no phone or email. BB and BR rows identify practitioners with residence-format streets and must not enter the shop-owner or contact path.
ownerSource: Verified free weekly Florida DBPR lic03bb.csv: only BS barbershop rows with a parseable person in address line 1 are owner candidates. BB and BR are barber-practitioner records, not barbershop ownership evidence.
phoneSource: None is currently verified and implemented for this route. The DBPR extract expressly has no phone or email; do not append, trace, or infer a private or direct-owner number from its names or streets.

workflow.label: Florida DBPR barbers extract
workflow.detail: Read only the verified free lic03bb.csv route; it supplies licence facts and no phone/email field.

workflow.label: Current Florida licence and class?
workflow.detail: Require current primary status, permitted secondary status, future expiry, and Florida state; only BS can continue to the owner-candidate decision.

workflow.label: Hold invalid licence
workflow.detail: Reject inactive, expired, out-of-state, or non-BS rows from this workflow.

workflow.label: BS owner named in address line 1?
workflow.detail: Accept only a parseable person as barbershop-owner candidate evidence; a street or business string is not a person.

workflow.label: Hold missing owner evidence
workflow.detail: Reject BS rows without a parseable person in address line 1.

workflow.label: BB or BR practitioner row
workflow.detail: Reject barber and restricted-barber rows from the shop-owner path; their record street may be residential and does not establish shop ownership.

workflow.label: Verified public business-contact source?
workflow.detail: No source is mapped today. Do not use the owner candidate, shop address, practitioner name, or residential street for append or trace processing.

workflow.label: Hold without contact source
workflow.detail: Keep BS identity evidence separate and do not create a contact candidate while no verified public business-contact source exists.

workflow.label: Business-contact and ownership gates
workflow.detail: If a permitted source is later mapped, require public business-contact provenance plus independent owner/handset evidence and normal line, DNC, suppression, and dedupe gates.

workflow.label: Hold unsupported contact
workflow.detail: Hold shared, private, unverified, non-compliant, or ownership-unsupported contacts.

workflow.label: Deliver supported classification
workflow.detail: Deliver only after a future public business-contact source and every required contact and owner-evidence gate pass.

edges.label: other class, inactive, expired, or out of state
all contact and owner-evidence gates pass
line, compliance, handset, or ownership evidence fails

failures.risk: BB or BR practitioner identity is presented as a barbershop owner.
failures.mitigation: Exclude BB/BR from barbershop_fl and retain no practitioner ownership inference.

failures.risk: A BB/BR residence-format street advances into parcel or trace work.
failures.mitigation: Do not persist the street for this workflow and fail closed before recipe-B trace processing.

failures.risk: A BS owner candidate is treated as a direct phone or handset owner.
failures.mitigation: The DBPR extract has no phone/email; hold the candidate until separately sourced public contact and independent evidence exist.

failures.risk: A street in BS address line 1 is parsed as an owner.
A published business line is relabeled as an owner line.
failures.mitigation: Require separately recorded public-contact provenance, line/compliance gates, and independent owner/handset evidence.

sources.label: Recipe-B home-street path

iterations.hypothesis: All current BS, BB, and BR records can be treated as owner-name candidates for recipe B.
iterations.test: Five-case audit selected from the existing eight-row fl_dbpr_barbers fixture and its actual parser/parcel tests on 2026-09-24: named BS, unnamed BS, BB residence, BR unit residence, and BR ordinary residence. No source request or provider call.
iterations.observed: Named BS becomes Owner/Barbershop with no street; unnamed BS is owner_not_named; BB and BR become Barber records with their record streets. homeStreetSource explicitly marks the Barber rows register-origin.
iterations.change: Restrict the proposed owner-shop intake to named BS rows, exclude BB/BR practitioners, and hold the job before any contact append or trace route.

measurement.result: Five bounded local parser/runtime branches were audited using the existing fixture; the actual targeted parser and parcel tests passed. This is code/fixture evidence only: no source-field coverage, phone value, mobile status, reachability, DNC result, ownership confirmation, or delivery outcome was measured.

cost.basis: Local fixture and runtime audit only; no paid discovery, append, trace, or phone verification was invoked.
cost.note: No clean delivered owner contact was measured. Historical brain expectations use another unverified denominator and are not a per-clean cost for this review.

implementation.summary: The adapter correctly distinguishes named BS owners from BB/BR practitioners, but the live recipe-B path admits practitioner residence streets and can progress to trace processing even though the source has no public business-contact field. A fail-closed source guard and BB/BR exclusion are required before this route can produce contact candidates.

nextMeasurement: Only after a legally eligible, verified public business-contact source is mapped, run a 5–20-record aggregate coverage audit with separate counts for current BS rows, parseable owner candidates, published business-contact fields, independently supported owners, authorized contact-gate passes, and deliveries. Exclude BB/BR and do not retain residential or private-contact data.
